_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: Separate userevents client + KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY for the User Event API (events group); a hand-authored second-key client
handfixes.why: KnowBe4 exposes two APIs behind one CLI: the Reporting API (KNOWBE4_API_KEY) and a separate User Event API on its own host with its own key (KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY). The `events` group (create/delete) talks to the User Event API via a dedicated hand-authored client package; the Reporting key cannot reach it. A reprint that drops the userevents package or its EnvKey breaks the events write surface.

handfixes.summary: `import` is a write but uses the MAIN Reporting key (flags.newClient), NOT the secondary User Event key; docs attribute keys per-write (4.34.2 renders no `import` for the all-GET Reporting spec; restated as: no Reporting key source reads the User Event key)
handfixes.why: The natural-but-wrong mental model is 'the events sub-product is the write surface, so all writes use the events key.' FALSE: `import` is a bulk POST write that uses the MAIN Reporting key (import.go calls flags.newClient(), the primary client) - only `events create`/`events delete` use the secondary key. Two adversarial rounds were needed to get the docs right (README + SKILL.md both initially mis-attributed). The governance Write row must keep `import` attributed to the main key (no secondary-key note) while `events create` notes it needs KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY.

asserts.contains: `events create` (push a custom risk event; needs `KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY`)

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For knowbe4 the manifest gained: KNOWBE4_BASE_URL, KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY. server.json gained: KNOWBE4_BASE_URL, KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: KNOWBE4_BASE_URL, KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name, and no file stores operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds; applied by tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. cliutil.RefuseHeld compares each operator-named write with every credential the secret funnel holds, in every view it decodes, and refuses a match before it is written: profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl and the learn tables (learnings, playbooks, candidates, recall misses, entity aliases, patterns). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: Neither KnowBe4 key reaches the other API's host. The credential kit binds each key to its own origin; a value held from two sources (a config file api_key equal to the User Event key) is bound to both, so each client also refuses a request that repeats the other API's effective keys whole, as written or percent-decoded, in the URL, any header or the body
handfixes.why: `KNOWBE4_API_KEY=ReportingSecret-7c92 KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY=EventSecret-8d31 events create ... --description ReportingSecret-7c92` posted the Reporting key to the User Event host: origin pinning checks where a request goes, not what it carries. The check is one shared matcher (cliutil.RequestRepeatsValues over EchoesValues and the outbound part reassembly) on a transport installed on both clients, with each client's foreign keys declared from their sources, never inferred from values. The Reporting set is every credential the configuration sends (key fields, auth header, credential-named configured headers, base URL userinfo password and credential query values): seen/r1-credential-to-other-api-host-whole-set-seen-failing.log. Codex review round 1 (knowbe4 4.34.2 reprint). Seen failing: seen/r1-credential-to-other-api-host-seen-failing.log; passing: seen/r1-credential-to-other-api-host-passing.log (run dir). (knowbe4 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: Every novel and insight reads a collection as complete only through one predicate, insights.CollectionSynced: the collection's own sync completion record (sync_state last_attempt_complete = 1, written only by a list walk that finished), never a row in its table. The phishing-test recipient walk keeps its own record (pst-recipients), set only when every test was walked over a completely synced set of tests and no later tests sync finished after it. freshness readiness, the QBR training completion share and the risk-leaderboard counts use the same predicate; `workflow archive --full` clears cursors without recording a completed sync (SaveSyncCursor, not SaveSyncState).
handfixes.why: One cached detail row was proof the whole collection was synced: after `training-enrollments get 1` (Bob's enrollment) and `sync --resources users,phishing-tests`, untrained-clickers listed Alice as untrained although her enrollment (status Passed) was never fetched; the same row made coverage-gaps, risk-leaderboard open_trainings, the QBR completion share and freshness readiness answer. A partial recipient walk (one test failed) was read as every recipient, and `workflow archive --full` wrote a completed record for every resource before walking any, so an archive stopped at its first resource left users and enrollments synced and empty (coverage-gaps answered no gaps). Codex review round 2 (knowbe4 4.34.2 reprint). Seen failing then passing: .review/seen-missing-input-read-as-zero.log (TestR2OneCachedRowIsNotASyncedCollection, TestR2FullArchiveRecordsNoSyncItDidNotFinish).

handfixes.summary: A value the local store holds in two places is read through one helper, insights.newer (over insights.newestReading): the reading taken from the API more recently wins, whichever source holds it. The QBR account risk score compares the account risk snapshots with the account table (an `account info` row); group-risk-contribution weights each group by the newer of the groups table's and its snapshots' member_count, null (never 0 or 1) when neither holds one. SnapshotRisk stamps each copied row with the time the row was read (its synced_at), never the sync's time, and puts every account reading on one series (AccountEntityID); risk-drift reads the account as one series and names an entity from its newest reading. Because snapshots carry each row's own read time, drift's input is counted per entity (driftHeld: some entity read at two different times), never across entities, in risk-drift, group-risk-contribution and freshness readiness.
handfixes.why: QBR always preferred the account snapshot over the account table without comparing freshness: after `sync` read current_risk_score 65 and a later `account info` stored 90, `qbr` reported 65. The sync also copied the stored account row into a snapshot stamped with the sync's own time, so after a later sync read 70 the copy of the older 90 tied with it and QBR reported 90. group-risk-contribution read a group missing from the groups table as 0 members although its snapshots carried member_count 50. Codex review round 2 (knowbe4 4.34.2 reprint). Seen failing then passing: .review/seen-stale-source-preferred.log (TestR2QBRReadsTheNewerAccountReading, TestR2GroupWeightReadsTheNewerMemberCount, TestR2AccountScoreReadsTheNewerSource). Follow-up in the same class: once snapshots carried each row's read time, one `sync --resources users` left the users and the account at two different snapshot times, and the store-wide distinct-time count let risk-drift answer [] (nothing moved) with no entity read twice (TestNoNovelReadsAMissingInputAsNone, TestR2DriftNeedsOneEntityReadTwice; same log).

handfixes.summary: Every config.toml write is judged whole by one combined check, persistedEchoesCredential: every field the write persists, header values included, marshaled as save() writes it, against every credential the configuration carries (persistGateCredentials: configCredentialValues plus ReportingCredentials, so the base URL's userinfo password and credential-named header values count too). The agentcookie-managed path runs it on every write and refuses; the unmanaged path drops every header when it fails. Header values alone are judged by the same set (headerHoldsCredential).
handfixes.why: Under the .agentcookie-managed marker, refuseCredentialInConfigFile checked each header value alone and then left the headers out of the combined check, so a held key split between a header value and another non-credential field was written: a marked 0600 config.toml with [headers] X-Tail="ujmikolp0987654321" and `KNOWBE4_API_KEY=<the 36-character test value> KNOWBE4_REGION=qazwsxedcrfvtgbyhn knowbe4-cli --config <it> auth set-token` wrote the key's prefix into template_vars.region beside its suffix. Unmanaged, a header repeating the base_url userinfo password was kept, because the header check's set held no URL credentials. Codex review round 2 (knowbe4 4.34.2 reprint). Seen failing then passing: .review/seen-persistence-gate-skipped-under-agentcookie.log (TestR2ConfigWriteJudgesEveryFieldTogether, TestR2AuthSetTokenUnderAgentcookieWritesNoSplitKey).

handfixes.summary: The same-key exemption of the Reporting client's foreign set reads only the credential that client actually sends, config.SentReportingCredentials (the Authorization header AuthHeader builds from the effective configuration, whole and without its scheme word, and the key or token it is built from): the effective User Event key is foreign to the Reporting host unless it is that sent credential, never because a configuration layer an environment value overrode also holds it. The User Event client's exemption stays its own effective KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY, and every Reporting credential (effective key, URL credentials, every layer) stays foreign to the User Event host.
handfixes.why: guardClient built the Reporting foreign set as otherThan(userEventCredentials(), ReportingCredentials(c.Config)), and ReportingCredentials walks every configuration layer: with a 0600 config file holding api_key="EventSecret-8d31", `KNOWBE4_API_KEY=ReportingSecret-7c92 KNOWBE4_USER_EVENT_API_KEY=EventSecret-8d31 knowbe4-cli --config <it> users list --status EventSecret-8d31` sent the User Event key to the Reporting host, because the overridden file value exempted it. Codex review round 2 (knowbe4 4.34.2 reprint), instance 1 only; the unparseable base_url password instance is classified non-blocking. Seen failing then passing: .review/seen-credential-to-other-api-host.log (TestR2EventKeyIsForeignUnlessItIsTheSentReportingKey).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (internal/credkit, vendored) is wired by hand: one credkit.Declarations literal in internal/credwire/declarations.go, credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) first in both mains and credkit.Exit at the end, and every sink routed through the kit (Reporting and User Event transports, file writes, the SQLite driver internal/credsql, the MCP server stdio, HTTP and tool results, child processes, the terminal check). The SQLite driver sets the MCP sql tool's value cap as each connection opens (sqlite.Limit cannot reach a kit-wrapped connection), and the read-only opens run "select 1" where they pinged (the kit's connection does not forward Ping).

handfixes.summary: The generated credentials merge line `c.Knowbe4ApiKey = creds.Knowbe4ApiKey` carries a gitleaks:allow comment
handfixes.why: gitleaks 8.18.4 (CI's pinned version) reads the selector creds.Knowbe4ApiKey after an ApiKey assignment as a generic API key: the digit in the vendor name lifts its entropy over the rule's floor, where siblings such as creds.AuvikApiKey stay under it. It is a struct field copy, not a literal, so the line is allowed in place rather than the whole rule widened.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
